notes: Forms that make two writings of one name compare equal: conventional English abbreviations of given names as found in sale catalogues and imprints (Thos. Agnew, Wm. Blake), a plural courtesy prefix for firms, the connective that an ampersand stands for, and legal-form suffixes that catalogues add or drop (Ltd, GmbH). Written by the assistant from general knowledge of British trade usage, not copied from any source; add to it as data shows the need. Applied to normalised keys only when comparing or indexing, never to what is published.
